mwt-card-005.front: How does a white tail run from danger?
mwt-card-005.back: Low, smooth gallop with the tail up. A mule deer stots on all 4 feet (85%).

mwt-card-008.front: Signs of a buck 4 years or older?
mwt-card-008.back: Deep chest, sagging belly, thick neck blending into shoulders, legs look short (65%).

mwt-card-010.front: How common are mule deer and white tail hybrids on the western Canadian prairies?
mwt-card-010.back: About 1% (85%, Russell and others 2021). Not sure what it is? Do not shoot.

mwt-card-011.front: Average live weight of a white tail buck and doe (Idaho)?
mwt-card-011.back: Buck about 91 kg (200 lb), doe about 57 kg (125 lb) (80%).

mwt-card-014.front: Region 3 Thompson resident white tail kills, 2024?

mwt-card-015.front: MU 3-27 white tails taken per year, 2020 to 2024?
mwt-card-015.back: About 97 to 145 a year; 133 in 2024, about 17% success (90%).

mwt-card-016.front: Is there a white tail season in Region 2 (Fraser Valley)?
mwt-card-016.back: No. The Region 2 white tailed deer bag is 0 (97%, page 14).

mwt-card-019.back: Northwest white tail, Odocoileus virginianus ochrourus (75%).

mwt-card-023.front: Why does a double lung hit kill fast?
mwt-card-023.back: Air enters the chest and the lungs collapse; the deer runs on stored oxygen, often 50 to 137 m (70%).

mwt-card-024.front: What covers the front of the lungs?
mwt-card-024.back: The shoulder blade, which slides with the leg (80%).

mwt-card-025.back: Up the back of the front leg, one third up the chest (75%).

<text x="170" y="70" font-size="15" fill="#6b5b4b">never lies</text>
<text x="118" y="94" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b">catches your scent far</text>
<text x="118" y="114" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#c0392b">Beat it: only with the wind</text>
</g>

mwt-card-043.front: Why does blaze orange look dull to deer?
mwt-card-043.back: 2 colour cones (blue, green), no red cone (85%).
mwt-card-043.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 392" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Colour as you see it and as a deer sees it, a rough picture. Orange looks dull to a deer, blue still stands out, and a bright wash may glow in ultraviolet. A still hunter in cover is hard to see; a moving one is seen fast. Colour is not the problem: motion and outline are (Tip).">
<rect width="400" height="392" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="200" y="26" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">What a deer sees</text>
<text x="143" y="54" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">You</text>
<g data-tip="Low light|In low light, deer are most sensitive to blue and blue green (80%). Their eyeshine is a reflective layer behind the retina." data-tip-dot="252,44">
<text x="229" y="54" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Deer</text>
</g>
<!-- row 1: blaze orange -->
<g data-tip="Blaze orange|Deer have no red cone, so blaze orange looks dull to them, close to grey or brown (75%)." data-tip-dot="384,70">
<rect x="8" y="62" width="384" height="52" rx="8" fill="#f4eedf"/>

</g>

mwt-card-045.front: What does an unsure white tail often do?
mwt-card-045.back: Circles downwind to smell you (Tip, widely reported).

<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="200" y="22" font-size="17" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">How a white tail checks a threat</text><rect x="30" y="40" width="200" height="44" rx="10" fill="#fffaf0" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="2.5"/><text x="130" y="68" font-size="15" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">Ears: odd sound</text><rect x="30" y="100" width="200" height="44" rx="10" fill="#fffaf0" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="2.5"/><text x="130" y="128" font-size="15" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">Head up, eyes lock on</text><rect x="30" y="160" width="200" height="44" rx="10" fill="#fffaf0" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="2.5"/><text x="130" y="188" font-size="15" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">Motion? Stamp, bob</text><rect x="30" y="220" width="200" height="44" rx="10" fill="#fffaf0" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="2.5"/><text x="130" y="248" font-size="15" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">Not sure? Circles</text><line x1="130" y1="84" x2="130" y2="98" stroke="#e8590c" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/><polygon points="130.0,98.0 126.1,89.9 133.9,89.9" fill="#e8590c"/><line x1="130" y1="144" x2="130" y2="158" stroke="#e8590c" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/><polygon points="130.0,158.0 126.1,149.9 133.9,149.9" fill="#e8590c"/><line x1="130" y1="204" x2="130" y2="218" stroke="#e8590c" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/><polygon points="130.0,218.0 126.1,209.9 133.9,209.9" fill="#e8590c"/><rect x="250" y="210" width="140" height="60" rx="10" fill="#fbe3d4" stroke="#e8590c" stroke-width="2.5"/><text x="320" y="236" font-size="15" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">Nose confirms:</text><text x="320" y="256" font-size="14" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">snort, flag, gone</text><line x1="232" y1="242" x2="248" y2="242" stroke="#e8590c" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/><polygon points="248.0,242.0 239.9,245.9 239.9,238.1" fill="#e8590c"/><text x="320" y="70" font-size="14" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">downwind to</text><text x="320" y="88" font-size="14" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">smell you (Tip)</text><path d="M232 236 C 300 230 330 160 320 98" fill="none" stroke="#8a9a6b" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><text x="200" y="292" font-size="14" fill="#6b4f35" text-anchor="middle">Ears and eyes raise doubt. mwt-card-046.front: Why sit high or in a dark blind?
mwt-card-046.back: Gets you out of the eye level scan of a horizontal pupil (Tip).
mwt-card-046.diagram:

mwt-card-047.front: Legal status of deer urine lures from outside BC?

mwt-card-048.front: A doe stamps and stares. What do you do?
mwt-card-048.back: Freeze. The stamp is a test to make you move (Tip).

mwt-card-049.front: How many white tail calls did Atkeson and others record?

mwt-card-050.front: Which call marks a dominant buck's challenge in the rut?

mwt-card-051.back: A long drawn out grunt a buck makes with a doe (70%).

mwt-card-052.front: Why does a white tail flag?
mwt-card-052.back: Debated: warn others, tell the predator it is seen, or guide fawns. One study found little support for warning others (70%).

mwt-card-053.front: Where does a spooked white tail run?
mwt-card-053.back: To the nearest thick cover, often stopping just inside to look back (Tip).

mwt-card-054.front: Penn State collar study: what did deer do on opening day?
mwt-card-054.back: Reacted the day before, then hid inside their home range (70%).

mwt-card-059.front: How many bedding areas did the average Mississippi collared buck use?
mwt-card-059.back: About 31 in a season; repeat beds had dense screening cover (65%).

mwt-card-060.front: White tail vs mule deer bucks: which fight more?
mwt-card-060.back: White tails (75%, Montana State University Extension). That is why rattling works.

mwt-card-063.front: How long is a newborn fawn hidden?

mwt-card-077.front: Do deer feed hard before a storm?
mwt-card-077.back: Penn State: no change before 30 winter storms; less movement during (80%).

mwt-card-078.front: Does the moon move white tails?
mwt-card-078.back: Collar studies: small or no effect; dawn and dusk win (75%).

mwt-card-079.front: How much water does a deer drink on dry food?
mwt-card-079.back: About 3 kg per kg of dry food (80%).

mwt-card-113.back: Unskinned tail plus a testicle or part of the penis (99%, page 15).
